SPI General Ledger (GL) Module — OVERVIEW Source: Sidat Hyder Financials Software Guide This section gives an overview of Sidat Hyder Financials, and how it can save your time and effort. **What is Sidat Hyder Financials?** Sidat Hyder Financials is an accounting system that can fully integrate your Sales, Purchase, Inventory, Fixed Assets and General Ledger systems. It is reliable and robust software that will adapt and expand as your business and accounting needs grow. Sidat Hyder Financials gives you the power and flexibility to work the way you want to. Sidat Hyder Financials is full of useful functions that provide solutions to your everyday Accounting problems. Sidat Hyder Financials allows the following: - User defined system configuration and setup - State of the art reporting - Budgeting and cost controls - Multi-currency - Security flexible data entry - Payments & withholding tax - Flexible data entry and - Much more... With an easy to use and intuitive Windows based interface, the system architecture is based on Client Server Technology and has been developed to work in an integrated environment.

Double click on the setup icon, the system will ask you for the destination drive on which you would like save the program -- select as desired.

SPI General Ledger (GL) Module — PROCESS Source: Sidat Hyder Financials Software Guide ### Process [Vouchers Verification:]{.underline} As the name of the option implies this option is used to verify or un-verify all entered vouchers before they are actually posted. Posting in the GL system basically refers to the concepts that after posting these vouchers are locked for any further process and cannot be un-posted. However, verified vouchers can be unverified though a verified voucher is functionally the same as a posted voucher except that it can be unlocked/unverified as opposed to a posted voucher, which is not reversible once the process has been applied. [Getting there;]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Verification. [Posting:]{.underline} The posting option basically locks the records for which posting is being run and updates posted balances while locking the posted voucher from undergoing any further modifications. [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Posting. This displays a list of all voucher types and corresponding vouchers that have been entered.

[Period End]{.underline} As the name of the option implies this option is provided to enable the user to close periods that fall within the financial year of the company. Please note that once the period has been closed no vouchers entered during that period may be modified or deleted. Similarly, any entry for the period is not allowed though you can view/take out reports for all entered transactions for the period. Before you close the period, make sure that you have posted all the vouchers that were entered during the period. SPI Support — Past Incident Log (Reference Examples) Incident #1042 Reported issue: Client's Inventory module showed negative stock for several SKUs after a bulk stock adjustment import. Root cause: The import file used a different UOM (units) than what was configured for those items in the Item Master, causing quantities to be misread by a conversion factor. Resolution: Reversed the bad import, corrected the UOM mapping in the import template, re-ran the import. Recommended client standardize UOM per item before any future bulk imports. SPI Support Knowledge Base — Inventory & Sync Incidents INCIDENT TYPE: Stock Count Mismatch Between Warehouses Symptoms: A client reports that the same item shows different stock quantities on two different screens (e.g., Stock Status Report vs. Warehouse Transfer screen). Root Cause (most common): An in-transit stock transfer between warehouses was left in "Pending Receipt" status and never confirmed at the destination warehouse. The source warehouse has already deducted the stock, but the destination hasn't received it yet, so the item appears to be "missing" from both counts temporarily. Resolution Steps: 1. Check Inventory > Transfers > Pending Receipts for any transfer involving the affected item. 2. If a transfer is stuck in Pending, confirm with the warehouse staff whether the physical stock actually arrived. 3. If it arrived, complete the receipt confirmation in SPI. If it did not arrive, escalate to warehouse operations — this is a physical logistics issue, not a software bug. INCIDENT TYPE: Reorder Point Not Triggering Purchase Suggestion Symptoms: Stock has fallen below the configured reorder point, but no suggested Purchase Order appears in Purchase > Suggested Orders. Root Cause (most common): The item's Replenishment Rule was configured with a "Preferred Supplier" left blank. SPI will not auto-generate a suggested PO without a preferred supplier assigned, even if the reorder point logic is otherwise correctly configured. Resolution Steps: 1. Navigate to Inventory > Configuration > Replenishment Rules for the affected item. 2. Confirm a Preferred Supplier is assigned. 3. If missing, assign one and re-run the nightly Reorder Suggestion job manually via Inventory > Utilities > Run Reorder Job Now. Escalate to Engineering only if: a preferred supplier is assigned and the item still doesn't generate a suggestion after a manual job run. INCIDENT TYPE: Barcode Scan Not Recognized During Stock Count Symptoms: Warehouse staff scan a barcode during a cycle count and get "Item Not Found," even though the item exists in the system. Root Cause (most common): The barcode printed on the physical label doesn't match the Bin Location code format configured in SPI (see Implementation Guide — Bin Location codes must follow AA-00-00 format). Older labels printed before a warehouse reconfiguration are a frequent cause of this after a client's warehouse layout changes. Resolution Steps: 1. Confirm the current Bin Location format under Inventory > Configuration > Warehouse Setup. 2. Compare against the physical label — if it doesn't match, the label needs to be reprinted, this is not a data or software issue. Escalate to Engineering only if: the label format matches the configured Bin Location format exactly and the scan still fails.

SPI Support Knowledge Base — Payroll & Access Incidents INCIDENT TYPE: Payroll Run Shows Incorrect Tax Deduction Symptoms: An employee's payslip shows a tax deduction that doesn't match expected values for their jurisdiction. Root Cause (most common): The employee's Tax Jurisdiction Code was changed mid-cycle (e.g., after a transfer between provinces/states) but the current payroll run was already in "Draft" status before the change, so it's still using the old jurisdiction's tax table. Resolution Steps: 1. Check Payroll > Employee Master for the affected employee's current Tax Jurisdiction Code. 2. If it was recently changed, the current draft payroll run must be discarded and regenerated — edits to jurisdiction do not retroactively apply to an already-drafted run. 3. Confirm with Finance before discarding a run if it has already been partially approved. Escalate to Engineering only if: the jurisdiction code is correct and was not recently changed, and the tax calculation still appears wrong. SPI Support Guide — Common Issues & Troubleshooting 1. Login / Session Issues Symptom: User reports being logged out repeatedly, or "session expired" errors within minutes of logging in. Common root cause: SPI session timeout is tied to system clock sync between the client's PowerBuilder terminal and the application server. If the terminal's local clock has drifted more than 5 minutes from the server, sessions expire early. First check: compare terminal system time to server time before escalating further. 2. Report Generation Failures Symptom: A report (e.g., Stock Status Report, Payroll Summary) fails to generate or returns a blank result, even though data clearly exists. Common root cause #1: The report's underlying DataWindow is filtering on a date range field that doesn't match the client's regional date format (DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY) — this silently returns zero rows instead of erroring. Common root cause #2: The report references a view that depends on both Oracle and SQL Server data (cross-database join).
